theme: artifact WAITFILE/WAITGONE human timeout + DEADLINE lease gate

tests.name: wait_hit
tests.cmd: touch then WAITFILE 500ms hit abs path

tests.name: gone_cycle
tests.cmd: WAITGONE present miss; rm then gone hit

weaknesses.title: Bad WAITFILE duration indistinguishable from timeout miss
weaknesses.detail: WAITFILE path 'nope' → OK=0 HIT=0 MS=0 same shape as missing file with zero elapsed. Agents cannot tell config error from absence without pre-PARSEMS.

weaknesses.title: DEADLINE sub-second human durations floor to 0s (instant expire)
weaknesses.detail: DEADLINE '500ms' → DEADLINE_SECS=0, due≈now, EXPIRED immediately. Sub-second wait leases unusable via duration form.

weaknesses.title: Bare numeric unit asymmetry: DEADLINE secs vs SLEEP ms
weaknesses.detail: DEADLINE 5 = +5 seconds; SLEEP 5 = 5 milliseconds. Same literal, 1000× different semantics. Human-string form reduces but bare nums remain traps.

weaknesses.title: WAITFILE hit LAST is path string not 1 alone
weaknesses.detail: OK and WAITFILE_HIT are reliable; LAST equals absolute path. Agents comparing LAST_N==1 after hit are wrong (path not numeric).

weaknesses.title: EXPIRED still clobbers LAST_N before REMAINING
weaknesses.detail: Must LET due_save; unchanged from prior iters.

weaknesses.title: No distinct err code for bad timeout vs miss
weaknesses.detail: last_err may differ but HIT/MS collapse; need WAITFILE_ERR class.
weaknesses.repro: compare last_err after nope vs missing

workarounds: Prefer duration strings over bare numbers for SLEEP/DEADLINE
language_gaps: WAITFILE distinct soft-fail for bad duration vs timeout
Unified bare-number unit policy or SLEEP_SEC / DEADLINE_MS flags
